transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Sofia (Lumina), Alan (Lumina CTO), Priya (Infra), Jonah (Procurement)
Shared artifacts: Redwood renewal deck (https://redwood.ai/decks/lumina-renewal-2025.pdf), latency spreadsheet (link shared in chat)

Summary:
Quick check-in focused on renewal timing, a new burst capacity SKU request, and adding two geographic regions (eu-west-1 + ap-southeast-1) with attention to data residency and SOC2 audit requirements. SE to run benchmarks; AE to update commercial options.

Topics:
- Contract extension length and pricing tradeoffs
- Dedicated/burst capacity vs hosted overage path
- Regional deployment, data residency, and KMS integration
- Procurement timeline and legal redlines
- Technical validation: latency/p95 & throughput targets

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, we'll keep this tight, roughly 45 minutes. Quick roll call?
[00:10] Sofia: Hi all, Sofia here.
[00:12] Alan: Alan, hi.
[00:13] Priya: Priya, Infra.
[00:15] Jonah: Jonah from procurement.
[00:16] Ethan: Ethan from Redwood, SE.
[00:18] Maya: Great. So agenda — renewal cadence, burst plan, and region add. I'll let Ethan kick off on the tech bits.
[00:30] Ethan: Cool. Last week we reviewed baseline numbers from your staging run. For the pilot you're seeing p95 of ~180ms in us-west under normal load, and the big ask is: how does that look in eu + apac when you go live and hit spikes.
[01:02] Sofia: Right, and to be explicit, our compliance team wants EU data at-rest to remain in eu-west-1, not cross-region, if possible. Also ap-southeast for our partners in SEA.
[01:20] Ethan: Understood. For data residency we have two options: private deployment into your VPC (on-prem/VPC) or a Redwood-hosted regional instance with KMS integration and audit logs. The hosted regional offers faster time-to-market.
[01:40] Priya: On the KMS note, we need Bring-Your-Own-Key and key rotation visibility — can you show that in the audit trail?
[01:52] Ethan: Yes, BYOK via customer KMS is supported and key usage shows in the audit logs; we can share sample logs. There's a small latency tax for off-HSM wrapping but usually negligible for inference.
[02:10] Maya: Commercially, Sofia, you mentioned wanting burst capacity for Q1 marketing pushes. Do you have a rough token spike profile?
[02:25] Sofia: Expect spikes up to 150k tokens/day for up to three days during a promo, base steady ~20k tokens/day. We want guaranteed headroom or a fast throttle policy.
[02:38] Maya: Good — we have a burst SKU that overlays on top of reserved capacity; it's billed as a short-term add-on. We'll include pricing in the updated quote.
[02:50] Jonah: On procurement, two asks: a) show 12 vs 24 month pricing, and b) can you give an explicit SLAs for regional failover? Our legal likes hard SLAs.
[03:05] Maya: We'll prepare both 12/24 scenarios and propose an SLA for regional failover; note that true automatic failover across regions depends on model replication and KV cache warming — we can offer a documented fallback policy.
[03:22] Ethan: Technically to avoid poor tail latency during failover we recommend warmed standby model replicas in the target region; that's extra reserved capacity but offers predictable p95 during failover windows.
[03:40] Alan: That makes sense. Can you quantify cost delta for warmed standby vs cross-region cold boot?
[03:50] Ethan: Off the cuff, warmed standby is roughly +25–40% on the reserved capacity line depending on instance type and quantization. Cold cross-region fallback will show higher transient latency and can spike token costs due to retries. We'll include a modeled example in the spreadsheet.
[04:12] Sofia: Another compliance item: SOC2 Type II — do you have the report and can we have an NDA-guarded copy?
[04:20] Maya: Yes, Redwood has SOC2; we'll share the report under an NDA.
[04:26] Priya: Does Redwood provide proof of encryption at rest for embeddings? Some of our PHI-adjacent vectors need to be treated carefully.
[04:36] Ethan: Embeddings are encrypted at rest; we can show KMS key IDs and linkage. There's occasional transcription errors in our docs where it says "embbeds" but the data is encrypted.
[04:48] Sofia: (laughs) noted.
[05:00] Ethan: For the benchmark plan — I'll run p95 and p99 across eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1. Can you confirm sample model and payload sizes?
[05:12] Priya: We'll provide a representative model (4B parameter LLM), prompt distribution, and a traffic replay file.
[05:20] Ethan: Great, that will help us simulate KV cache hit rates. On quantization — are you comfortable with int8 variants for cost savings?
[05:30] Alan: We need to validate output quality. If there's any regression we can't accept it blindly. We'll require A/B eval on key prompts.
[05:40] Ethan: Agreed. Part of Redwood Optimize is a recommendation layer for quantization thresholds and we can run small evals.
[05:48] Jonah: From procurement side — any legal redlines we should know of? We have a standard review that flags data residency, liability cap, and export controls.
[06:00] Maya: Noted. We'll ask legal to prepare redline-friendly language. Usually liability caps are negotiable for enterprise.
[06:12] Sofia: Timeline — we want to be live in eu by end of Jan 2026. That gives us roughly ten weeks to finalize contracts and perform validation. Is that feasible?
[06:24] Ethan: From infra perspective, yes if we lock the model version and access patterns soon; the benchmarking + prod validation usually takes 4–6 weeks.
[06:32] Maya: So high level: commercial decision by mid-November to hit Jan go-live is doable. Jonah, is that consistent with procurement windows?
[06:40] Jonah: Yes, mid-November sign is ok if we have final SOW and pricing by Oct 24.
[06:48] Maya: We'll aim for Oct 17 to send pricing and Oct 21 for benchmarks — gives you buffer.
[07:00] Ethan: Technical Q: do you plan to use Redwood Dedicated or hosted with regional tenancy?
[07:08] Priya: Prefer hosted regional to avoid heavy ops, but if we need strict network isolation we might ask for Dedicated.
[07:18] Ethan: The dedicated option offers VPC peering and private subnets; hosted regional is faster to onboard and supports BYOK + audit logs. Tradeoff is isolation vs time-to-market.
[07:34] Alan: Can we start hosted regional and move to Dedicated later if needed?
[07:40] Ethan: Yes, migration path exists but requires model re-provisioning and KV cache seeding; there will be a short validation window. We can document the steps.
[07:52] Sofia: Cost question — if we commit to 24 months, what's the delta on reserved instance pricing?
[07:58] Maya: Typical is 10–18% off list depending on committed volume and whether you include a burst plan. We'll provide explicit numbers in the quote.
[08:08] Jonah: Also call out any early termination fees.
[08:12] Maya: Will do.
[08:20] Ethan: For benchmarks I'll simulate spikes up to 200k tokens/day to validate burst SKU behavior and measure p95/p99.
[08:30] Priya: We'll share the traffic replay and model by EOD tomorrow.
[08:36] Ethan: Great.
[08:40] Sofia: A couple of smaller items: SSO (SAML) for the console, RBAC so our operators can't accidentally change model pins, and longer log retention for 6 months. Can you support those?
[08:52] Ethan: SAML SSO is supported; RBAC is part of the console. Log retention is configurable — default is 90 days but enterprise can extend to 6+ months for an add-on.
[09:05] Sofia: Perfect.
[09:10] Maya: Any competitor constraints? Are you running parallel evals?
[09:14] Sofia: We're also testing Anthropic for some use cases and running Bedrock perf numbers. Primary tie-breaker is predictable unit economics and regional availability.
[09:26] Ethan: Understood. We'll make sure the modeled economics are clear.
[09:34] Alan: Can Redwood provide a short runbook for post-deploy emergency rollback? We need to know steps in case of model regression.
[09:42] Ethan: Yes, standard runbook includes immediate pin to prior model version, traffic weight rollback, and fallback to a smaller quantized variant. We'll include it.
[09:52] Maya: Ok let's move to quick recap and next steps.
[09:58] Ethan: Benchmarks: I'll run eu/apac tests and share p95/p99 and raw logs by Oct 21.
[10:06] Maya: Commercial: I'll send 12/24 month pricing and burst SKU by Oct 17 and include potential warmed-standby cost scenarios.
[10:14] Priya: We'll send traffic replay and model by Oct 15.
[10:20] Jonah: Procurement aims for final sign by mid-Nov if numbers look good.
[10:24] Sofia: And we'll review SOC2 under NDA — please share.
[10:30] Maya: Noted. Anything else?
[10:34] Alan: No, that's it.
[10:36] Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with the attachments and action items.

End of meeting.

Notes on transcription quirks: speaker labels swapped briefly at 05:00–05:20 in auto-transcript, occasional mis-heard 'KV cahce' instead of KV cache, 'Redwoood' typo seen in one line.

References mentioned in call:
- Renewal/commercial deck: https://redwood.ai/decks/lumina-renewal-2025.pdf
- Latency spreadsheet (privileged link sent in chat)
- SOC2 report: to be shared under NDA

Checklist (quick):
- Pricing scenarios (12/24) sent by 2025-10-17
- Benchmarks (eu/apac) shared by 2025-10-21
- Procurement timeline confirmed by Lumina by 2025-10-20
